executive_assessment.text: The Dry Corridor evidence links erratic rain and production stress with food and schooling coping, without municipal incidence estimates.
Bilwi/Waspam information channels and Alal conflict displacement add local FCV context; neither establishes that climate caused armed violence or that radio closure measurably reduced adaptation.
SINAREM launch and WFP plan priorities are institutional/design evidence, not verified performance.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2026-04-23 reports: IACHR identifies Nicaragua’s Dry Corridor as 63 municipalities (37% of territory), reliant partly on subsistence/small-scale farming; 2024 El Niño intensified drought and reduced rain, harming crop output and food security.

Source dated 2026-04-23 reports: In the Dry Corridor, below-average and erratic rain reduced production and deepened household food insecurity; vulnerable families reduced food quantity or quality and withdrew children from school.
IACHR's 2025 report documents the September 2023 closure of Bilwi/Waspam Indigenous radios serving 17 territories, including channels for reporting violence and climate/environment concerns.

Source dated 2025-08-25 reports: IACHR reports an armed-settler attack on Mayangna Alal (Sauni As, 30 km from Bonanza, Bosawás) in January 2020: at least four killed, over 16 homes burned, survival goods looted and 79 families displaced.

The IACHR annual chapter names 63 Dry Corridor municipalities but does not identify which municipalities or report local household rates; it does not attribute a particular event to climate change.
No inspected report attributes armed-settler violence or displacement to a climate hazard; the Dry Corridor and Caribbean Coast findings should not be combined into an inferred causal chain.

The IACHR documents climate/environment information and violence-reporting roles of closed Indigenous radios but does not assess effects on preparedness or adaptation. SINAREM is described at launch/design stage, without independent operational-coverage or effectiveness evidence.
